title: two arms pass under BSD tools and fail on every Ubuntu run -- a GNU stat -f read as an mtime, and a parent-process refutation the CI checkout path satisfies -- so v0.1.8's tag reads red on test-only defects
body:
FOUND 2026-09-26 on CI, run 36230655008 (main at b4eed88, Ubuntu leg), during the 0.1.8 cut. Every local run is macOS, so neither the final suite (2040 of 2040) nor the cut's own test all (2040 of 2040) could see it.

WHAT HAPPENS. Two arms that pass under BSD tools fail on every Ubuntu run. Neither is a defect in devbin's code; both are the test's own spelling.

- fullcycle.bats, "cargo_build_dir asks cargo from the crate's directory, offline, and leaves Cargo.lock as it was (0150)". It read Cargo.lock's mtime as `$(stat -f %m f 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y f)`. GNU's `stat -f` is filesystem status: it prints that block to stdout and returns 1, so the one `$()` captured the block, free-block counts included, ahead of the epoch, and the counts differ between the two reads. The epoch itself was identical (1790412934 both times). This is the trap cmd/fleet's mtime_epoch already documents and avoids by capturing each spelling alone.
- dispatch.bats, "a declared option named directly replaces the dispatcher as a launcher must, and inside all it returns (0128)". It refuted a bare `bin/devbin` in the parent process's command line, to show the option was exec'd. On the runner the parent is bats's own exec, whose path is /home/runner/work/devbin/devbin/tests/..., and `devbin/devbin` contains `bin/devbin`.

WHO IT REACHES. devbin's own CI only; nothing ships in these files to an estate. But v0.1.8's tag carries both, so the tag's Ubuntu leg reads red on test-only defects while the code it tests is sound.

THE FIX. The mtime arm takes each stat spelling alone, as mtime_epoch does, and only a number is an answer. The parent arm refutes `bin/devbin clean`, which only the dispatcher as parent can produce (the dispatcher's own line carries the verb), and its inside-all half asserts the same string, so the two halves test one thing; driven, the dispatcher's parent line does contain it. Verified on Linux only once a push lets CI run it.

THE CLASS, for hv. The convergence loop runs on macOS alone, so a GNU-versus-BSD spelling in a test is invisible until CI after landing, as shellcheck was until the cut's lint gate. devbin-cc is drafting how the loop meets GNU tools and shellcheck before landing.

## Resolution

Fixed at 8a464a8. Test-only: no shipped file changes, so it reaches no estate, and the next release carries it.

- WHAT CHANGED. fullcycle.bats' Cargo.lock arm takes each stat spelling alone and accepts only a number, as cmd/fleet's mtime_epoch does, so GNU's filesystem-status block can no longer be read as an mtime. dispatch.bats' exec arm refutes `bin/devbin clean`, the dispatcher's own line with its verb, where a bare `bin/devbin` matched CI's checkout path; its inside-all half asserts the same string, and driven, the dispatcher as parent does carry it.
- ON CI. v0.1.8's tag run 36234487733 failed exactly these arms: 400 on Ubuntu AND macOS (the macOS runner's checkout, /Users/runner/work/devbin/devbin, contains `bin/devbin` too, where a local checkout at Devel/prj/Devbin does not), and 770 on Ubuntu. Main's run 36235749975 at 8a464a8: Ubuntu green, 2040 arms, both fixed arms passing. Its macOS leg is skipped on a push by design, and a dispatched macOS run could not be started: the account's Actions spending limit was reached (the run's own annotation says so), which hv is to clear. 400's cause and fix are the same on both runners, so the next macOS run -- a tag or a dispatch -- is its proof there.
- REVIEWS. vc, 2026-09-26: found on CI, both causes read from the logs and the arms, the narrowed refutation driven for strength, both arms ok alone. devbin-cc read the fix read-only and agreed on all three causes.
- THE CLASS. The convergence loop runs on macOS alone and on paths that never contain `devbin/devbin`, so neither GNU tools nor CI's paths reached it before landing; devbin-cc has drafted how the loop meets GNU tools, for hv.
